title: Math arXiv daily — 2026-10-23 announcement batch — 10 papers
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking of notable recent papers, not measured popularity; citation and independent-attention evidence is sparse for this newly announced batch.

sections.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's L² conjecture
sections.abstract: For every d≥2 and 0≤σ<1/3, the authors construct, with LLM assistance, a smooth bounded nonnegative lens-type potential with arbitrarily small stated weighted L² and supremum norms for which −Δ+V has only pure point spectrum at positive energies, contradicting Simon's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that for each d≥2 and 0≤σ<1/3 there is a smooth bounded V≥0 with arbitrarily small ‖V‖∞ + ∫R^d |x|^(1−d+σ)|V(x)|² dx such that −Δ+V has pure point spectrum in (0,∞), disproving Simon's stated absolutely-continuous-spectrum conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schrödinger operators on R^d, all d≥2, with weighted-integrability exponent 0≤σ<1/3; the asserted potential is smooth, bounded and nonnegative.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an unrefereed preprint and its elaborate multiscale construction has not been independently proof-checked here; the authors explicitly disclose LLM assistance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main theorem claims a counterexample to a named spectral conjecture for every d≥2 and is cross-listed in spectral theory and mathematical physics; the introduction states the potential construction and spectral-averaging route.

sections.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
sections.abstract: The author characterizes exactly when all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators on a Hardy model space have bounded symbols: precisely when the defining inner function has a connected sublevel set at some level in (0,1), with linked embedding, weak-factorization and de Branges-space consequences.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space has a bounded symbol iff its nonconstant defining inner function is one-component; the paper also gives a sharp logarithmic loss in a quantitative symbol-norm bound and related de Branges results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Hardy model spaces defined by a nonconstant inner function; one-component means that one sublevel set {z: |Θ(z)|<t} is connected for some 0<t<1.
sections.unique_caveat: The author says the complete results were first posted on 2026-10-07 under DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23214254; this arXiv announcement is a delayed deposit, not a newly obtained result. The main characterization concerns Hardy model spaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a necessary-and-sufficient geometric characterization resolving a named bounded-symbol conjecture and, by known equivalences, two related conjectures; it is cross-listed across functional and complex analysis and has an earlier public DOI.

sections.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed–Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
sections.abstract: For full-length Reed–Solomon codes, the author classifies deep holes at interpolation degrees k+m for every finite field when m=3,4,5,6,7, and proves additional field-size-dependent exclusions and classifications for all m≥3.
sections.claimed_result: For m=3,…,7 the only deep-hole exceptions are the specified Segre and Frobenius-power families (at m=4,6, respectively, in dimension two over characteristic-two fields); for general m≥3 the paper proves uniform exclusion/classification results under explicit field-size conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full-length RS_q(k) evaluated over all of F_q; received words whose interpolation polynomial has degree k+m, with m≥3 and k+m≤q−1. Unconditional classification is for m=3,…,7; broader statements require stated field-size bounds.
sections.unique_caveat: The results concern the specified interpolation-degree ranges, not every deep hole for every code parameter. The paper also discusses recent parallel work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main theorem gives unconditional finite-field classifications for five consecutive excess degrees, with uniform bounds beyond them; the paper bridges coding theory, combinatorics and number theory and includes reproducible finite certificates for remaining small cases.

sections.title: Exact controllability and rapid stabilization of linear difference delay equations and one-dimensional hyperbolic systems
sections.abstract: For finite pointwise-delay systems, the authors establish a necessary-and-sufficient Hautus-type frequency criterion for exact controllability in every L^r, 1≤r<∞, answer a prior conjecture, and derive rapid-stabilization and one-dimensional hyperbolic-system consequences.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove necessity, complementing known sufficiency, of a Hautus-type criterion for exact controllability in L^r; they further show it suffices for arbitrarily fast exponential stabilization in L² and extend the criterion to one-dimensional linear hyperbolic PDEs.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Linear difference-delay systems with finitely many pointwise delays, 1≤r<∞; the PDE application is to one-dimensional linear hyperbolic systems reducible to those delay systems.
sections.unique_caveat: Rapid stabilization is established as a sufficient consequence of the exact-controllability criterion, not as a necessary-and-sufficient stabilization characterization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors explicitly identify and resolve a prior conjecture on necessity of the controllability criterion for r>1; the result connects control theory with PDE through the method of characteristics.

sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: For a planar thrackle, where every pair of edges meets exactly once, the author proves an upper bound of floor(4(n−1)/3) edges on n≥4 vertices by combining a computer-assisted small-case verification with a discharging argument.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that every thrackle on n≥4 vertices has at most floor(4(n−1)/3) edges.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A thrackle is a plane drawing of a graph in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing; the bound is for n≥4 vertices.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is weaker than Conway's conjectured n-edge bound, so the conjecture remains open; the proof uses computer-assisted verification for graphs with at most twelve vertices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It gives a concrete new upper bound on a named longstanding extremal-graph conjecture and is cross-listed in combinatorics and two geometry/topology areas; its proof combines finite computation with structural embedding arguments.

sections.title: A sharpened L8_t L4_x-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
sections.abstract: The author proves that even-function extremizing sequences for the one-dimensional L8_t L4_x Strichartz inequality approach a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense, via an optimal-constant inequality conjectured by Gonçalves.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the conjectured inequality with its optimal constant and shows that every extremizing sequence of even L²(R) data approaches a centered Gaussian in the paper's stated sense.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The one-dimensional L8_t L4_x Strichartz estimate for nonzero even initial data in L²(R); the stability assertion is restricted to even extremizing sequences.
sections.unique_caveat: The symmetry restriction is essential to the stated result; the abstract does not assert this stability for nonsymmetric extremizing sequences.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper resolves a named 2019 inequality conjecture with the optimal constant and derives a stability/rigidity statement for extremizing sequences; it is cross-listed in classical analysis and PDE.

sections.title: Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
sections.abstract: For every finite p, the author constructs a forced one-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson problem with two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions sharing zero initial data and uniformly L^p-bounded spatial densities, while uniqueness holds in the bounded-density class described in the paper.
sections.claimed_result: The author constructs a nonnegative ion density smooth for positive times and source S∈C([0,1];L¹(R²)), S(0)=0, for which two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions in C([0,1];L¹(R²)) share zero initial data and have spatial densities uniformly bounded in each prescribed finite L^p(R); uniqueness holds when spatial density is bounded and the electric field is Lipschitz.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Forced Vlasov–Poisson equation on the one-dimensional whole space over [0,1], with the source and solution classes stated above; the counterexample reaches every finite density exponent p but not the bounded-density endpoint.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a forced-equation construction; it does not by itself establish nonuniqueness for the unforced equation or other solution classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper supplies a nonuniqueness counterexample together with a contrasting uniqueness statement at bounded density, making the regularity threshold mathematically explicit.

sections.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
sections.abstract: For counts of a fixed connected regular graph in sparse random regular graphs, the authors derive upper-tail large-deviation rates and conditioned structures in two asymptotic regimes, with a distinct cycle rate and structure caused by the degree constraint.
sections.claimed_result: For connected Δ-regular H, the authors obtain upper-tail speed and rate for copies in G_n^d when np^(Δ/2)≫(log n)^(1/(v_H−2)) and p=d/n≪1. For Δ≥3 the rate matches Erdős–Rényi; for cycles the rate differs and conditioned graphs contain disjoint clique-/biclique-like structures with high probability. In a complementary strictly balanced-graph regime, they prove matching Erdős–Rényi rates and that almost all conditioned unlabeled copies are edge-disjoint.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed connected Δ-regular graph H, sparse random d-regular graph G_n^d, p=d/n→0. The first regime is np^(Δ/2)≫(log n)^(1/(v_H−2)); the complementary regime is 1≪n^(v_H)p^(e_H)≪(log n)^(α*_H/(α*_H−1)) for strictly balanced H; cycles (Δ=2) are treated separately.
sections.unique_caveat: The asymptotic conclusions are regime-dependent; neither rate functions nor conditioned structures should be extrapolated beyond the hypotheses stated in the paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives both a rate-function result and a structural description conditioned on a rare event, and it identifies where regular-graph behavior agrees with or differs from Erdős–Rényi; it is cross-listed in probability and combinatorics.

sections.title: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
sections.abstract: For a smooth hyperkähler fourfold with Picard group generated by a nef, nontrivial, non-big line bundle of nonnegative Kodaira dimension, the authors prove that some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration and establish supporting unobstructedness and smoothing results.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give a geometric proof that if X is a smooth hyperkähler fourfold, Pic(X)=Z[L], and L is nef, nontrivial, not big, with κ(L)≥0, then a positive multiple of L defines a Lagrangian fibration.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth hyperkähler fourfold; Picard group generated by the specified line bundle L; L nef, nontrivial, not big, and of nonnegative Kodaira dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is conditional on κ(L)≥0 and the Picard-rank-one hypothesis; it does not prove semiampleness for arbitrary hyperkähler manifolds or line bundles.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main statement is a semiampleness/fibration theorem under geometric hypotheses, supported by two additional tools the authors identify as independently useful; it bridges algebraic, complex and differential geometry.

sections.title: A unified quantitative approach to Chiti and Kohler–Jobin inequalities
sections.abstract: The authors prove quantitative stability versions of Chiti's reverse Hölder and Kohler–Jobin inequalities for first Dirichlet eigenvalues, controlling eigenfunction distance to the ball optimizer and a resolvent distance, respectively.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the Chiti deficit controls, up to translations, the L^q distance between a bounded-domain first eigenfunction and that of a ball with the same first eigenvalue for every 1≤q<p<∞; they also give a quantitative Kohler–Jobin estimate using the L∞→L² distance between Dirichlet resolvents.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: First Dirichlet eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of bounded domains; the first stability result assumes 1≤q<p<∞ and compares after translations, while the second concerns the stated resolvent norm.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimates are tied to these first-eigenvalue inequalities and norms; they are not a general stability theorem for arbitrary spectral data or domains.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It supplies two quantitative refinements of classical spectral/rearrangement inequalities and is cross-listed between PDE and spectral theory; one estimate is uniform over every 1≤q<p<∞.
